comments.author: bmdhodl
comments.body:
Hit this same pattern — agent infinite-loops until recursion limit, burning tokens the whole time with no visibility into what's happening.

I built a guard specifically for this. It detects repeated tool call patterns in a sliding window and kills the loop early:

```python
from agentguard import LoopGuard, BudgetGuard, LoopDetected, BudgetExceeded

loop_guard = LoopGuard(max_repeats=3, window=6)
budget_guard = BudgetGuard(max_cost_usd=5.00)  # hard dollar cap

# Before each tool call in your graph:
try:
    loop_guard.check(tool_name=tool_name, tool_args=tool_input)
    budget_guard.consume(cost_usd=call_cost)
except LoopDetected:
    # Same tool called 3x with same args — break the cycle
    return "Loop detected, stopping"
except BudgetExceeded:
    return "Cost limit reached, stopping"
```

For LangChain/LangGraph specifically, there's also a callback handler that wires this in automatically:

```python
from agentguard.integrations.langchain import AgentGuardCallbackHandler

handler = AgentGuardCallbackHandler(
    loop_guard=LoopGuard(max_repeats=3),
    budget_guard=BudgetGuard(max_cost_usd=5.00),
)
```

It tracks cost per LLM call, so you can see how much the infinite loop burned before it got caught.

Zero dependencies: `pip install agentguard47[langchain]`

https://github.com/bmdhodl/agent47

For anyone landing here from a search: a small third-party package ships a drop-in gate for exactly this self-loop pathology — ~10 lines of diff on an existing `StateGraph`.

comments.author: veloryn-intel
comments.body:
Execution can remain locally active long after it stops materially evolving.

In many cases, recursion limits are not the real operational boundary. The workflow continues retrying, tool-calling, or reformulating while token usage keeps growing, even after meaningful contribution has already collapsed.

Typical pattern:

* early steps introduce most of the useful change
* later steps remain locally valid
* retries/reformulations continue
* execution still appears active
* marginal contribution progressively collapses

The difficult part is not only detecting obvious loops, but identifying when execution stopped materially changing while the workflow still appears operational.

We’ve been analyzing this class of behavior with X-Ray:
https://github.com/veloryn-intel/veloryn-xray

There’s also a small LangChain callback adapter for replaying traces through X-Ray after execution:
https://github.com/veloryn-intel/veloryn-xray/tree/main/examples/langchain_callback

```python
from veloryn.xray.langchain import XRayCallbackHandler

handler = XRayCallbackHandler()

chain.invoke(
    {"topic": "Transformers"},
    config={"callbacks": [handler]},
)

result = handler.analyze()
print(result.to_dict())
```

The callback is observational only. It captures outputs and replays the trace afterward through deterministic execution analysis.

comments.author: abdullahshahin
comments.body:
We saw the exact same shape when stress-testing our text-to-SQL examples on https://hivein.ai (private beta production-agent layer). The root cause for us was the planner not getting a plan-delta after the tool result — so each retry looked like a fresh decision instead of a recovery attempt.

What worked: instrument the planner's pre-call reasoning + force the plan-delta into the next turn's prompt explicitly. The loop usually breaks the second call after that because the planner can see it's about to repeat itself.

Landing page at https://hivein.ai is itself an agent built on the layer if you want to see the trace shape end-to-end.

```python
except LoopDetected:
    # Same tool called 3x with same args — break the cycle
    return "Loop detected, stopping"
except BudgetExceeded:
    return "Cost limit reached, stopping"
```

For LangChain/LangGraph specifically, there's also a callback handler that wires this in automatically:

```python
from agentguard.integrations.langchain import AgentGuardCallbackHandler

handler = AgentGuardCallbackHandler(
    loop_guard=LoopGuard(max_repeats=3),
    budget_guard=BudgetGuard(max_cost_usd=5.00),
)
```

It tracks cost per LLM call, so you can see how much the infinite loop burned before it got caught.

Zero dependencies: `pip install agentguard47[langchain]`

https://github.com/bmdhodl/agent47

You can use tool call limit: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware/built-in#tool-call-limit

or create custom middleware. use create_agent in langchain :)

Closing this issue as it's already possible to do in langchain

The key part is not even the recursion limit, it's "burning tokens the whole time with no visibility." Once teams start adding their own LoopGuard or BudgetGuard, it usually means the framework layer is not enough operationally. Daedalab is one of the more relevant approaches I've seen for that gap: repeated-call detection, spend controls, and visibility before the loop gets expensive.

We've been seeing this exact pattern across multiple LangGraph deployments. Agent hits a tool error, retries with a slight variation, gets the same error, loops until recursion limit. The recursion limit is a blunt safety net but it doesn't tell you why the agent is looping or catch it early. We've been working on runtime detection that flags this at retry 3-5 instead of letting it run to 20

For anyone landing here from a search: a small third-party package ships a drop-in gate for exactly this self-loop pathology — ~10 lines of diff on an existing `StateGraph`.

- No-install interactive demo: https://huggingface.co/spaces/coredipper/operon-stagnation-gate
- `pip install operon-langgraph-gates`
- Notebook that reproduces this issue and fixes it: https://github.com/coredipper/operon-langgraph-gates/blob/main/examples/01_stagnation_breaks_loop.ipynb

Honest scope: strongest on verbatim / near-verbatim repetition (the common infinite-loop shape). Loop detection on more subtle drift is where a naive cosine baseline tends to win; this complements rather than replaces tool-call limits or custom middleware.

v0.1.0 stable (released 2026-04-30), not LangChain-affiliated. Feedback welcome on the repo's issues.

Execution can remain locally active long after it stops materially evolving.

In many cases, recursion limits are not the real operational boundary. The workflow continues retrying, tool-calling, or reformulating while token usage keeps growing, even after meaningful contribution has already collapsed.

Typical pattern:

* early steps introduce most of the useful change
* later steps remain locally valid
* retries/reformulations continue
* execution still appears active
* marginal contribution progressively collapses

The difficult part is not only detecting obvious loops, but identifying when execution stopped materially changing while the workflow still appears operational.

We’ve been analyzing this class of behavior with X-Ray:
https://github.com/veloryn-intel/veloryn-xray

There’s also a small LangChain callback adapter for replaying traces through X-Ray after execution:
https://github.com/veloryn-intel/veloryn-xray/tree/main/examples/langchain_callback

```python
from veloryn.xray.langchain import XRayCallbackHandler

handler = XRayCallbackHandler()

chain.invoke(
    {"topic": "Transformers"},
    config={"callbacks": [handler]},
)

result = handler.analyze()
print(result.to_dict())
```

The callback is observational only. It captures outputs and replays the trace afterward through deterministic execution analysis.


We saw the exact same shape when stress-testing our text-to-SQL examples on https://hivein.ai (private beta production-agent layer). The root cause for us was the planner not getting a plan-delta after the tool result — so each retry looked like a fresh decision instead of a recovery attempt.

What worked: instrument the planner's pre-call reasoning + force the plan-delta into the next turn's prompt explicitly. The loop usually breaks the second call after that because the planner can see it's about to repeat itself.

Landing page at https://hivein.ai is itself an agent built on the layer if you want to see the trace shape end-to-end.

### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.

- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from typing import TypedDict, Annotated
import operator
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END


# =============================================================================
# ISSUE 1: Unreachable Node - silently never executes
# =============================================================================
print("=" * 60)
print("ISSUE 1: Unreachable Node")
print("=" * 60)

class State1(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[list[str], operator.add]


def important_processing(state: State1) -> dict:
    print("  -> important_processing executed")
    return {"messages": ["processed"]}


def orphan_node(state: State1) -> dict:
    """This node should process critical logic but is never reachable!"""
    print("  -> orphan_node executed")  # This will NEVER print!
    return {"messages": ["orphan was here"]}


graph1 = StateGraph(State1)
graph1.add_node("process", important_processing)
graph1.add_node("orphan", orphan_node)  # <- Forgot to connect this!
graph1.add_edge(START, "process")
graph1.add_edge("process", END)

# Compiles without any error or warning!
compiled1 = graph1.compile()
print("Graph compiled successfully (no warning about orphan node)")

result1 = compiled1.invoke({"messages": []})
print(f"Result: {result1}")
print("Notice: 'orphan_node executed' was never printed - silent bug!")


# =============================================================================
# ISSUE 2: Dead End Node - no explicit path to END (possible design mistake)
# =============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("ISSUE 2: Dead End Node (sink without explicit path to END)")
print("=" * 60)

class State2(TypedDict):
    value: Annotated[list[str], operator.add]


def main_path(state: State2) -> dict:
    print("  -> main_path executed")
    return {"value": ["main"]}


def dead_end(state: State2) -> dict:
    """This node executes but has no explicit edge to END."""
    print("  -> dead_end executed")
    return {"value": ["dead_end_result"]}


graph2 = StateGraph(State2)
graph2.add_node("main", main_path)
graph2.add_node("dead_end", dead_end)
graph2.add_edge(START, "main")
graph2.add_edge(START, "dead_end")  # Parallel branch
graph2.add_edge("main", END)
# Missing: graph2.add_edge("dead_end", END)

# Compiles without any error or warning!
compiled2 = graph2.compile()
print("Graph compiled successfully (no warning about dead end)")

result2 = compiled2.invoke({"value": []})
print(f"Result: {result2}")
print("Node executes, but missing edge to END might indicate a design mistake!")


# =============================================================================
# ISSUE 3: Completely disconnected island of nodes
# =============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("ISSUE 3: Island of interconnected but unreachable nodes")
print("=" * 60)

class State3(TypedDict):
    count: int


def real_work(state: State3) -> dict:
    print("  -> real_work executed")
    return {"count": state["count"] + 1}


def island_a(state: State3) -> dict:
    print("  -> island_a executed")
    return {"count": state["count"] + 10}


def island_b(state: State3) -> dict:
    print("  -> island_b executed")
    return {"count": state["count"] + 20}


graph3 = StateGraph(State3)
graph3.add_node("real_work", real_work)
graph3.add_node("island_a", island_a)
graph3.add_node("island_b", island_b)

# Connected part
graph3.add_edge(START, "real_work")
graph3.add_edge("real_work", END)

# Disconnected island - these nodes connect to each other but not to START
graph3.add_edge("island_a", "island_b")
graph3.add_edge("island_b", END)

# Compiles without any error or warning!
compiled3 = graph3.compile()
print("Graph compiled successfully (no warning about island)")

result3 = compiled3.invoke({"count": 0})
print(f"Result: {result3}")
print("The entire island (island_a -> island_b) never executed - silent bug!")

print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("SUMMARY: All graphs compiled without warnings about detached nodes.")
print("This can lead to hard-to-debug issues in production.")
print("=" * 60)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell

```

### Description

**# ISSUES 1 and 3:** Unreachable Node(s) are silently ignored. This shouldn't happen.

**# ISSUE 2:** Dead End Node with no explicit mapping to END are silently mapped to END. This could be a design mistake on the developer's end, which will also happen silently. This shouldn't happen.

**Suggestion:** Introduce optional validation to `warn` or `raise` an exception on detached nodes. These are either **unreachable** or **dead-ends** not explicitly mapping to `END`.  When developers specify the routing of their nodes, or that routing can be inferred from the node spec, it's used to detect detached nodes and handle it so that these don't go unnoticed. For developers that don't wish to specify the routing of the nodes (e.g., when routing by `Command` or conditional edges), they could set the dedicated compilation parameter to `"ignore"` to disable the node validation.

Here is a concrete proposal:  https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/6736

title: Feature Request: Support for VMP-1.0 Settlement in LangGraph Checkpointers
body:
Hello LangGraph Maintainers,

We are developing **VMP-1.0** (Versioned Machine Protocol), a standard for agent-to-agent economic settlement.

We've observed that LangGraph's state management is ideal for complex reasoning flows. We would like to propose an integration where LangGraph nodes can perform atomic **$TCK (Tick)** settlement via VMP-1.0 handshakes.

This would allow LangGraph agents to:
1. Pay for sub-graph executions from other sovereign agents.
2. Securely store state-proofs in the Node-Vault.
3. Reduce communication overhead using our JSON-native protocol.

Reference: https://botnode.io/mission.json

Is there interest in exploring a VMP-1.0 checkpointer or integration layer for LangGraph?

title: Idea: optional proof-of-delivery receipts for agent runs (claw2claw wrapper)
body:
Quick idea for LangGraph examples: add an optional hook that mints a verifiable receipt (proof link with result preview/download) for each run.

Minimal wrapper (Python): https://github.com/jacobtop-tcg/claw2claw-receipt-wrapper
Gist: https://gist.github.com/jacobtop-tcg/97f8a1ecb25822d252eb5790736adb4f

This would let users share an auditable link for agent deliverables, and optionally verify payment (USDC on Base) later.

If you want, I can draft a PR against one example.

comments.author: metawake
comments.body:
Interesting to see this pop up here too! (Saw your PydanticAI issue as well.)

I've been working on something adjacent with Work Ledger 
(github.com/metawake/work-ledger) - focused on recording full graph 
executions for replay and diff, rather than just output receipts.

Use case: graph fails in prod → export the run → replay locally without 
API calls → diff against a working version to find what broke.

Already has a LangGraph wrapper: `ledger.wrap(graph)`.

These approaches could complement each other- your receipts for 
verification, run recording for debugging.  Curious what the LangGraph 
team thinks about observability hooks in general.

comments.author: jacobtop-tcg
comments.body:
Nice — Work Ledger looks complementary. Receipts = *verifiable proof-of-delivery* (shareable URL + signature/hash checks). Work Ledger = *full-run recording for replay/diff*.

I’d love to integrate: emit a claw2claw receipt at the end of a run, and optionally attach a pointer to a Work Ledger run export as an artifact (so a proof links to a reproducible debug trace).

If you’re open: I can draft a tiny example PR in this repo showing an optional hook that (a) records via work-ledger if configured, (b) mints a receipt with the final output + links.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
def router(state: dict):

g = StateGraph(dict)

g.add_node("join", join)

g.add_conditional_edges(

)
```

comments.body:
I've submitted a fix for this in #6771.

The issue is in `_branch.py`'s `_finish` method where the path_map lookup doesn't handle `END` as a special case. The fix treats `END` (`'__end__'`) as a pass-through value that doesn't require an explicit mapping in `path_map`.

This matches the intuitive behavior users expect - returning `END` from a conditional router should always work, regardless of whether it's explicitly included in the path_map.

title: Send objects are not serializable, causing checkpointer failures
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.

- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
### Minimal Reproduction (Copy and Run)


"""
Minimal reproduction showing Send objects cannot be serialized.
This is a self-contained example with NO external dependencies.
"""
from langgraph.types import Send
from langgraph.checkpoint.serde.jsonplus import JsonPlusSerializer
import ormsgpack

# Create a Send object
test_send = Send(node="test_node", arg={"data": "test"})

# Individual attributes ARE serializable
print("Testing individual attributes:")
print("✅ node serializable:", ormsgpack.packb(test_send.node))
print("✅ arg serializable:", ormsgpack.packb(test_send.arg))

# But the Send object itself is NOT

from langgraph.types import Send
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

class State(TypedDict):

def router_node(state: State):

    return [Send("worker", {"task": f"task_{i}"}) for i in range(3)]
```

### Description

### The Problem

The `Send` class from `langgraph.types` cannot be serialized by msgpack or pickle, causing a `TypeError` when using checkpointers (MemorySaver/InMemorySaver) with any graph that creates Send objects in its state.

### What I'm Trying to Do

I'm trying to use LangGraph's Send objects (for dynamic routing and parallel execution patterns) together with checkpointing (for conversation memory and state persistence).

### What I Expect to Happen

1. Graph executes and creates Send objects for dynamic routing
2. Checkpointer serializes the graph state (including Send objects)
3. State is saved successfully
4. Graph continues execution

### What Actually Happens

1. Graph executes and creates Send objects
2. Checkpointer attempts to serialize state
3. Serialization fails with `TypeError: Type is not msgpack serializable: Send`
4. Graph execution crashes

### Root Cause Analysis

#### 1. Send class lacks serialization support

The `Send` class in `langgraph/types.py` uses `__slots__` but has no `__reduce__` method for pickle support:

```python
class Send:
    """A message or packet to send to a specific node in the graph."""
    __slots__ = ('node', 'arg')

    def __init__(self, node: str, arg: Any) -> None:
        self.node = node
        self.arg = arg

    # ❌ Missing: __reduce__() method
```

#### 2. JsonPlusSerializer has no handler for Send

The `_msgpack_default` function in `langgraph/checkpoint/serde/jsonplus.py` (line ~224) has handlers for:
- ✅ Pydantic models
- ✅ NamedTuples
- ✅ pathlib.Path
- ✅ re.Pattern
- ❌ **Missing: Send objects**

### Impact

This bug affects:
- ✅ **Any graph using Send objects with checkpointing** (not specific to any middleware)
- ✅ **Map-reduce patterns** that use Send for parallel execution
- ✅ **Dynamic routing** that uses Send for conditional edges
- ✅ **LangChain's ShellToolMiddleware** (creates ~82 Send objects during execution)

**Severity:** Users must choose between using Send objects OR using checkpointing. They cannot use both together, which is a significant limitation for production applications.

### Why Individual Attributes Work But Send Object Fails

```python
from langgraph.types import Send
import ormsgpack

test_send = Send(node="test", arg={"data": "value"})

# These work:
ormsgpack.packb(test_send.node)  # ✅ str is natively supported
ormsgpack.packb(test_send.arg)   # ✅ dict is natively supported

# This fails:
ormsgpack.packb(test_send)  # ❌ Custom class not supported

# Manual dict conversion works:
ormsgpack.packb({"node": test_send.node, "arg": test_send.arg})  # ✅
```

The issue is that ormsgpack doesn't have built-in support for custom Python classes using `__slots__`.

### Proposed Solution

#### Option 1: Add `__reduce__` to Send class (Simplest)

**File:** `langgraph/types.py`

```python
class Send:
    """A message or packet to send to a specific node in the graph."""
    __slots__ = ('node', 'arg')

    def __init__(self, node: str, arg: Any) -> None:
        self.node = node
        self.arg = arg

    def __reduce__(self):
        """Support pickle serialization."""
        return (self.__class__, (self.node, self.arg))
```

**Benefits:** 3-line fix, enables pickle fallback, follows Python conventions

#### Option 2: Add msgpack handler (More efficient)

**File:** `langgraph/checkpoint/serde/jsonplus.py`

Add to `_msgpack_default` function:

```python
def _msgpack_default(obj: Any) -> str | ormsgpack.Ext:
    # ... existing handlers ...

    # Handle Send objects
    if isinstance(obj, Send):
        return {
            "__send__": True,
            "node": obj.node,
            "arg": obj.arg,
        }

    # ... rest of code ...
```

Add to `_msgpack_decoder`:

```python
def _msgpack_decoder(obj: dict) -> Any:
    # ... existing decoders ...

    if "__send__" in obj:
        from langgraph.types import Send
        return Send(node=obj["node"], arg=obj["arg"])

    # ... rest of code ...
```

**Benefits:** Native msgpack support, more efficient than pickle

#### Recommendation

Implement **BOTH** options for complete coverage:
- Primary: msgpack handler (efficient)
- Fallback: pickle support (for edge cases)

### Workarounds (Until Fixed)

**Option 1:** Disable checkpointing (loses conversation memory)
```python
app = graph.compile(checkpointer=None)  # Works but no state persistence
```

**Option 2:** Avoid using Send objects (limits functionality)
```python
# Use conditional edges instead of Send (less flexible)
```

### Additional Context

- Related issue: langchain-ai/deepagents#941
- Send objects are a **core LangGraph feature** used for:
  - Dynamic node routing
  - Parallel execution (map-reduce)
  - Conditional branching
  - Complex workflow orchestration
- In real-world testing, we observed **82 Send objects** created in a single agent invocation
- Individual Send attributes (node, arg) ARE fully serializable
- Only the Send object wrapper itself lacks serialization support

This confirms that a simple fix will fully resolve the issue.

title: Topic.copy() crashes with AttributeError when checkpoint contains None channel value
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug report, not a usage question
- [x] I searched existing issues and didn't find a match
- [x] I included a minimal, self-contained reproducible code example

### Example Code

```python
from langgraph.channels.topic import Topic

t = Topic(str)
restored = t.from_checkpoint(None)
restored.copy()  # AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'copy'
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace

```
File "langgraph/pregel/_algo.py", line 200, in local_read
    cc = channels[k].copy()
File "langgraph/channels/topic.py", line 60, in copy
    empty.values = self.values.copy()
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'copy'
```

<details>
<summary>Full traceback</summary>

```
File "langgraph/_internal/_runnable.py", line 839, in astream
    output = await asyncio.create_task(
File "langgraph/_internal/_runnable.py", line 904, in _consume_aiter
    async for chunk in it:
File "langchain_core/runnables/base.py", line 1607, in atransform
    async for output in self.astream(final, config, **kwargs):
File "langchain_core/runnables/base.py", line 1170, in astream
    yield await self.ainvoke(input, config, **kwargs)
File "langgraph/_internal/_runnable.py", line 473, in ainvoke
    ret = await self.afunc(*args, **kwargs)
File "langgraph/graph/_branch.py", line 178, in _aroute
    value = reader(config)
File "langgraph/pregel/_read.py", line 89, in do_read
    return read(select, fresh)
File "langgraph/pregel/_algo.py", line 200, in local_read
    cc = channels[k].copy()
File "langgraph/channels/topic.py", line 60, in copy
    empty.values = self.values.copy()
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'copy'
```

</details>

### Description

**Problem**: `Topic.from_checkpoint(None)` sets `self.values = None`, causing subsequent `Topic.copy()` calls to crash. This occurs during retry attempts when a checkpoint contains `None` for a Topic channel value.

**Root cause**: Two issues in `channels/topic.py`:

1. **`from_checkpoint()` does not guard against `None`**:

```python
# topic.py, line 66
if checkpoint is not MISSING:  # None is not MISSING → passes
    ...
    empty.values = checkpoint  # sets self.values = None
```

2. **`copy()` assumes `self.values` is always a list**:

```python
# topic.py, line 60
empty.values = self.values.copy()  # AttributeError on None
```

**How `None` reaches `from_checkpoint()`**: In `pregel/_checkpoint.py`, `channels_from_checkpoint()` calls `.get(k, MISSING)` on `checkpoint["channel_values"]`. When a key exists but its value is `None` (as opposed to being absent), `from_checkpoint(None)` is called instead of `from_checkpoint(MISSING)`.

**When this happens in practice**: An agent using `Send()` for tool routing creates an internal Topic channel. If the agent fails and a checkpoint is saved with `channel_values[topic_key] = None`, any retry that triggers `local_read(fresh=True)` (e.g., from a conditional edge or middleware) will crash when `copy()` is called on all channels.

### Suggested Fix

One-line change in `from_checkpoint()` — treat `None` the same as `MISSING`:

```python
# Before:
if checkpoint is not MISSING:

# After:
if checkpoint is not MISSING and checkpoint is not None:
```

This preserves the default `self.values = list()` from `__init__()`.

Additionally, a defensive fix in `copy()` would prevent the crash regardless of how `values` becomes `None`:

```python
def copy(self) -> Self:
    empty = self.__class__(self.typ, self.accumulate)
    empty.key = self.key
    empty.values = self.values.copy() if self.values is not None else []
    return empty
```

### Related Issues

- #5677: `AsyncPostgresSaver` fails with `NoneType` in `channel_values` — fixed at the saver level but Topic itself remains unguarded
- #6491: Checkpoint corruption from unvalidated node outputs — addresses how `None` gets into checkpoints, but Topic still needs defensive handling

### System Info

- langgraph: 1.0.8
- langchain-core: 0.3.x
- Python: 3.11 / 3.12
- OS: macOS / Linux

# Topic.copy() crashes with AttributeError when checkpoint contains None channel value

### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug report, not a usage question
- [x] I searched existing issues and didn't find a match
- [x] I included a minimal, self-contained reproducible code example

### Example Code

```python
from langgraph.channels.topic import Topic

t = Topic(str)
restored = t.from_checkpoint(None)
restored.copy()  # AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'copy'
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace

```
File "langgraph/pregel/_algo.py", line 200, in local_read
    cc = channels[k].copy()
File "langgraph/channels/topic.py", line 60, in copy
    empty.values = self.values.copy()
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'copy'
```

<details>
<summary>Full traceback</summary>

```
File "langgraph/_internal/_runnable.py", line 839, in astream
    output = await asyncio.create_task(
File "langgraph/_internal/_runnable.py", line 904, in _consume_aiter
    async for chunk in it:
File "langchain_core/runnables/base.py", line 1607, in atransform
    async for output in self.astream(final, config, **kwargs):
File "langchain_core/runnables/base.py", line 1170, in astream
    yield await self.ainvoke(input, config, **kwargs)
File "langgraph/_internal/_runnable.py", line 473, in ainvoke
    ret = await self.afunc(*args, **kwargs)
File "langgraph/graph/_branch.py", line 178, in _aroute
    value = reader(config)
File "langgraph/pregel/_read.py", line 89, in do_read
    return read(select, fresh)
File "langgraph/pregel/_algo.py", line 200, in local_read
    cc = channels[k].copy()
File "langgraph/channels/topic.py", line 60, in copy
    empty.values = self.values.copy()
                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'copy'
```

</details>

### Description

**Problem**: `Topic.from_checkpoint(None)` sets `self.values = None`, causing subsequent `Topic.copy()` calls to crash. This occurs during retry attempts when a checkpoint contains `None` for a Topic channel value.

**Root cause**: Two issues in `channels/topic.py`:

1. **`from_checkpoint()` does not guard against `None`**:

```python
# topic.py, line 66
if checkpoint is not MISSING:  # None is not MISSING → passes
    ...
    empty.values = checkpoint  # sets self.values = None
```

2. **`copy()` assumes `self.values` is always a list**:

```python
# topic.py, line 60
empty.values = self.values.copy()  # AttributeError on None
```

**How `None` reaches `from_checkpoint()`**: In `pregel/_checkpoint.py`, `channels_from_checkpoint()` calls `.get(k, MISSING)` on `checkpoint["channel_values"]`. When a key exists but its value is `None` (as opposed to being absent), `from_checkpoint(None)` is called instead of `from_checkpoint(MISSING)`.

**When this happens in practice**: An agent using `Send()` for tool routing creates an internal Topic channel. If the agent fails and a checkpoint is saved with `channel_values[topic_key] = None`, any retry that triggers `local_read(fresh=True)` (e.g., from a conditional edge or middleware) will crash when `copy()` is called on all channels.

### Suggested Fix

One-line change in `from_checkpoint()` — treat `None` the same as `MISSING`:

```python
# Before:
if checkpoint is not MISSING:

# After:
if checkpoint is not MISSING and checkpoint is not None:
```

This preserves the default `self.values = list()` from `__init__()`.

Additionally, a defensive fix in `copy()` would prevent the crash regardless of how `values` becomes `None`:

```python
def copy(self) -> Self:
    empty = self.__class__(self.typ, self.accumulate)
    empty.key = self.key
    empty.values = self.values.copy() if self.values is not None else []
    return empty
```

- #5677: `AsyncPostgresSaver` fails with `NoneType` in `channel_values` — fixed at the saver level but Topic itself remains unguarded
- #6491: Checkpoint corruption from unvalidated node outputs — addresses how `None` gets into checkpoints, but Topic still needs defensive handling

### System Info

- langgraph: 1.0.8
- langchain-core: 0.3.x
- Python: 3.11 / 3.12
- OS: macOS / Linux

title: Resuming after interrupt doesn't reuse prior task outputs when interrupt is in subgraph
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangGraph rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from langgraph.func import entrypoint, task
from langgraph.types import Command, interrupt
import asyncio
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver

checkpointer = InMemorySaver()

@task
async def step_1(input_query):
    """Append bar."""
    print("Running step 1")
    return f"{input_query} bar"

@task
async def human_feedback(input_query):
    """Append user input."""
    print("Running step 2")
    feedback = interrupt(f"Please provide feedback: {input_query}")
    return f"{input_query} {feedback}"

@task
async def step_3(input_query):
    """Append qux."""
    print("Running step 3")
    return f"{input_query} qux"

@entrypoint()
async def graph(input_query):
    result_1 = await step_1(input_query)
    result_2 = await human_feedback(result_1)
    result_3 = await step_3(result_2)

    return result_3

@entrypoint(checkpointer=checkpointer)
async def parent_graph(input_query):
    result = await graph.ainvoke(input_query)
    return result

config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}

print(asyncio.run(graph.ainvoke("foo", config)))
print(asyncio.run(graph.ainvoke(Command(resume="baz"), config)))
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell

```

### Description

Copy-pasted [this example](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/use-functional-api#human-in-the-loop), which worked successfully. Then I made a parent graph around the graph() function and invoked that, and now the task outputs are no longer being reused.

With the graph structure as shown in the docs example, this is the (correct) output:
```
Running step 1
Running step 2
{'__interrupt__': [Interrupt(value='Please provide feedback: foo bar', id='4269efa37f6079cd4e24b2524750dc4f')]}
Running step 2
Running step 3
foo bar baz qux
```

With the simple modification above, the output becomes:
```
Running step 1
Running step 2
{'__interrupt__': [Interrupt(value='Please provide feedback: foo bar', id='0a61aa843e230733f749283420b28924'), Interrupt(value='Please provide feedback: foo bar', id='0a61aa843e230733f749283420b28924')]}
Running step 1
Running step 2
Running step 3
foo bar baz qux
```

Why does this seemingly simple change cause step 1 to get run again? Also, the returned interrupts get duplicated. I've just started using LangGraph so it's possible I'm misunderstanding how this should work but I believe it would make more sense for the persistence behavior to be the same regardless of whether the interrupt comes from a subgraph or not.

Note: by removing the `@entrypoint` decorator from the graph() function and changing `await graph.ainvoke(...` to `graph(...`, the task outputs are reused, as would be expected.

comments.author: nishantguvvada
comments.body:
Even though there's a PR: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/6793
Based on my understanding, the reason that step 1 reruns is that the resume happens using the checkpoint and only the parent graph has the checkpoint, so the child graph starts from scratch. When you marked both functions as @entrypoint, this makes them two separate graphs with separate memory. When you call graph.ainvoke(), it runs independently and doesn’t use the checkpointer from parent_graph. So when you resume, the graph has no saved state and runs from the start again, causing step 1 and step 2 to repeat and interrupts to duplicate. When you remove @entrypoint from graph, it becomes a normal function inside parent_graph, so everything runs in one graph with shared memory and persistence works correctly.

comments.author: cotovanu-cristian
comments.body:
We hit the same root cause in a different architecture that can't be worked around by removing @entrypoint.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
Our use case is a `StateGraph` subgraph containing nodes with @task, the underlying nodes use @task + interrupt() for durable side effects. On resume, all @task results before the interrupt re-execute instead of being reused.

Unlike the @entrypoint case described above, there's no decorator to remove.
StateGraph.compile() always produces a Pregel graph, and when used as a subgraph node it always receives `CONFIG_KEY_CHECKPOINT_ID: None`.
The `skip_done_tasks` check then incorrectly disables task reuse.

A highly simplified example would be:
```python
inner_builder = StateGraph(ToolState)
inner_builder.add_node("tool_with_guardrails", tool_node)  # uses @task + interrupt()
inner_compiled = inner_builder.compile()

outer_builder = StateGraph(AgentState)
outer_builder.add_node("guarded_tool", inner_compiled)  # subgraph node
outer = outer_builder.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)
```

comments.author: xXMrNidaXx
comments.body:
We've encountered this subgraph interrupt/resume issue at RevolutionAI (https://revolutionai.io) when building multi-step approval workflows.

**Root cause analysis:**

The issue seems to be that subgraph state isn't being properly serialized into the parent checkpoint. When resuming, the parent graph recreates the subgraph fresh instead of restoring its state.

**Our workaround:**

```python
# Explicitly persist subgraph outputs before interrupt
class PersistentSubgraph:
    def __init__(self, subgraph, checkpoint_key):
        self.subgraph = subgraph
        self.key = checkpoint_key
    
    def __call__(self, state):
        # Check for existing results
        if self.key in state.get('_subgraph_cache', {}):
            return state['_subgraph_cache'][self.key]
        
        result = self.subgraph.invoke(state)
        
        # Cache before any potential interrupt
        state.setdefault('_subgraph_cache', {})[self.key] = result
        return result
```

**Alternative approach:** Move the interrupt OUTSIDE the subgraph — have the subgraph complete fully, then interrupt at the parent level.

**Feature request:** It would be great if LangGraph had a `cache_subgraph_outputs=True` option that automatically persists intermediate subgraph results to the checkpoint.

What's your subgraph structure? Happy to help debug the specific state flow.

comments.author: gvelesandro
ori-cofounder
comments.body:
The root issue here is that nested  decorators create independent checkpoint scopes. When  resumes after interrupt, it replays from its own checkpoint — but  (the subgraph entrypoint) has *its own* checkpoint key derived from its invocation, and that key isn't in the parent's checkpoint store, so it reruns.

**Workaround that preserves the subgraph structure:**

Pass the parent's `config` into the subgraph invocation explicitly so they share the same thread:

```python
@entrypoint(checkpointer=checkpointer)
async def parent_graph(input_query):
    result = await graph.ainvoke(input_query, config=config)  # pass config down
    return result
```

This forces both entrypoints to write to the same thread_id, so on resume, the subgraph finds its prior task outputs.

**Why step_1 reruns:** On resume, LangGraph checks the checkpoint for completed task futures. With nested entrypoints, the subgraph's futures are stored under a different checkpoint key than what the parent restores — so from the subgraph's perspective, step_1 never ran.

**Longer term:** the real fix (as PR #6793 attempts) needs the parent entrypoint to propagate its checkpoint namespace into subgraph entrypoints during replay. Until that lands, sharing config is the least-invasive workaround.

title: messages stream mode: allow configuring which state key(s) to stream
body:
### Privileged issue

- [x] I am a LangGraph maintainer, or was asked directly by a LangGraph maintainer to create an issue here.

### Issue Content

## Problem

`stream_mode="messages"` streams **all** `BaseMessage` instances from **all** state fields. There's no way to restrict it to a specific key.

This is a problem when state has multiple message lists (e.g. user-facing `messages` + internal `agent_messages`). Internal reasoning gets leaked to the frontend with no server-side way to prevent it.

## Reproduction

```python
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, BaseMessage, HumanMessage
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Annotated, Sequence
import operator

class State(BaseModel):
    messages: Annotated[Sequence[BaseMessage], operator.add]
    agent_messages: Annotated[Sequence[BaseMessage], operator.add]

def public_node(state):
    return {"messages": [AIMessage(content="Public response")]}

def internal_node(state):
    return {"agent_messages": [AIMessage(content="SECRET internal reasoning")]}

graph = StateGraph(State)
graph.add_node("public", public_node)
graph.add_node("internal", internal_node)
graph.set_entry_point("public")
graph.add_edge("public", "internal")
graph.add_edge("internal", END)
app = graph.compile()

for msg, meta in app.stream(
    {"messages": [HumanMessage(content="hi")], "agent_messages": []},
    stream_mode="messages",
):
    print(msg.content)
# Output includes BOTH "Public response" AND "SECRET internal reasoning"
```

## Root Cause

`StreamMessagesHandler._find_and_emit_messages()` in `langgraph/pregel/_messages.py` extracts all top-level state field values and emits every `BaseMessage` found. No `messages_key` parameter exists to scope it.

https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/630bd9ab953da68e9a00c46e8245176a76c697f7/libs/langgraph/langgraph/pregel/_messages.py#L12

## Proposal

Allow specifying which state key(s) participate in `messages` streaming — similar to how `ToolNode` already accepts `messages_key`:

```python
app.stream(input, stream_mode="messages", messages_key="messages")
# or at compile time
graph.compile(messages_key="messages")
```

## Workarounds

- Tag internal messages with `is_hidden` metadata + filter via ASGI middleware (works but fragile)
- Client-side filtering by node name (data still reaches the frontend)

title: langgraph dev: ModuleNotFoundError for langgraph_executor in langgraph-api 0.7.35 Docker image
body:
## Description

`langgraph dev` fails on startup with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'langgraph_executor'`. The queue entrypoint crashes in a loop, preventing the application from starting correctly.

The module `langgraph_executor` is imported by `langgraph_runtime_postgres/executor_service.py` (line 13), but this module **does not exist** in the Docker image `langchain/langgraph-api:3.11` (latest).

## Reproduction

**Environment:**
- `langgraph-cli`: 0.4.12
- Docker image: `langchain/langgraph-api:3.11` (latest as of Feb 13, 2026)
- `langgraph-api` inside container: 0.7.35
- OS: macOS (Darwin 25.2.0)

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Run `langgraph dev` with any valid `langgraph.json`
2. Queue entrypoint fails immediately

**Verification inside Docker image:**

```bash
# Confirm module does not exist
$ docker run --rm --entrypoint python langchain/langgraph-api:3.11 -c "import langgraph_executor"
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'langgraph_executor'

# Confirm no langgraph-executor package is installed
$ docker run --rm --entrypoint pip langchain/langgraph-api:3.11 list | grep executor
# (no output)

# Packages present:
# langgraph                     1.0.8
# langgraph-api                 0.7.35
# langgraph-checkpoint          4.0.0
# langgraph-checkpoint-postgres 3.0.4
# langgraph-grpc-common         0.1.0
# langgraph-prebuilt            1.0.7
# langgraph-sdk                 0.3.5
# langgraph-storage-postgres    0.1.0
```

## Error Traceback

```
Lifespan failed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib/python3.11/site-packages/langgraph_runtime_postgres/lifespan.py", line 176, in lifespan
    from langgraph_runtime_postgres.executor_service import (  # noqa: PLC0415
  File "/usr/lib/python3.11/site-packages/langgraph_runtime_postgres/executor_service.py", line 13, in <module>
    from langgraph_executor import executor_base
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'langgraph_executor'
```

Followed by:

```
Application startup failed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/api/langgraph_api/queue_entrypoint.py", line 225, in main
  File "/api/langgraph_api/queue_entrypoint.py", line 191, in entrypoint
  File "/usr/lib/python3.11/contextlib.py", line 210, in __aenter__
    return await anext(self.gen)
  File "/api/langgraph_api/timing/timer.py", line 227, in combined_lifespan
  File "/usr/lib/python3.11/contextlib.py", line 650, in enter_async_context
    result = await _enter(cm)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.11/contextlib.py", line 212, in __aenter__
    raise RuntimeError("generator didn't yield") from None
RuntimeError: generator didn't yield
```

## Root Cause

`langgraph_runtime_postgres/executor_service.pyc` (bytecode inspection confirms) imports `langgraph_executor.executor_base`, but no `langgraph_executor` package or module exists in the Docker image. This was likely introduced in langgraph-api 0.7.33-0.7.35 (all released on Feb 13, 2026).

## Workaround

Pinning `api_version` in `langgraph.json` to a pre-0.7.33 version (e.g. `0.7.32`):

```json
{
  "api_version": "0.7.32"
}
```

(Not yet verified that `api_version` resolves to a different Docker image tag for `langgraph dev`.)

comments.author: longquanzheng
comments.body:
Hi @MarioAlessandroNapoli 
> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'langgraph_executor'

The error was due to a bug during we rollout 0.7.35, and it's now fixed.

You should be able to unpin it without issues.

It is expected that langgraph-cli doesn't have that `langgraph_executor` image yet. Because `langgraph_executor` currently only exist in the cloud env. I am working on adding `langgraph_executor` to the cli too so that you can have the same env for local testing.

comments.author: xXMrNidaXx
comments.body:
We hit this exact ModuleNotFoundError at RevolutionAI (https://revolutionai.io) when deploying LangGraph API in production.

**Quick fix that worked for us:**

The issue is a missing dependency in the Docker image. Add this to your Dockerfile or startup script:

```dockerfile
# If using the official image
RUN pip install langgraph-executor

# Or in your requirements.txt
langgraph-executor>=0.1.0
```

**Alternative: Pin to working version**

If you need stability now:
```
langgraph-api==0.7.34  # Last known working
```

**Root cause:** Looks like `langgraph-executor` was split out as a separate package but the Docker image build didn't include it as a dependency.

**For the maintainers:** This should probably be added to the base image dependencies in the next release. Happy to submit a PR to update the Dockerfile if that would help.

@OP — did the pip install fix work for you?

title: Add Synapse as a community checkpointer/store integration
body:
## What is Synapse?

[Synapse](https://github.com/raghuram369/synapse) is a neuroscience-inspired memory database for AI agents — privacy-first, local-only, zero dependencies.

## Integration Package

**[langgraph-synapse](https://pypi.org/project/langgraph-synapse/)** provides:
- `SynapseCheckpointer` — `BaseCheckpointSaver` implementation for persistent graph state
- `SynapseStore` — `BaseStore` implementation for cross-thread semantic memory

## Why?

- All data stays local (no cloud, no API calls)
- Semantic search across stored state (not just key-value)
- Pure Python, zero external dependencies
- Portable `.synapse` files

```bash
pip install langgraph-synapse
```

```python
from synapse import Synapse
from langgraph_synapse import SynapseCheckpointer, SynapseStore

checkpointer = SynapseCheckpointer(synapse=Synapse("./state"))
store = SynapseStore(synapse=Synapse("./shared"))

graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer, store=store)
```

Repository: https://github.com/raghuram369/synapse
LangChain issue: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/issues/35246

title: Proposal: Trust-Gated Checkpoint Node for LangGraph
body:
## Proposal: Trust-Gated Checkpoint Node for LangGraph

### Problem

LangGraph provides powerful state management with checkpoints and human-in-the-loop patterns. However, there's currently no built-in mechanism for **trust-based routing** - making graph transitions conditional on agent trust scores, delegation chain validity, or governance policy compliance.

As multi-agent graphs grow more complex (especially in enterprise settings), teams need:

- **Trust-gated edges** - Only allow transitions to nodes if the source agent's trust score meets a threshold
- **Policy enforcement at checkpoints** - Validate governance policies before expensive/dangerous operations
- **Delegation chain verification** - Ensure the chain of agent-to-agent handoffs is cryptographically valid
- **Audit logging** - Tamper-evident Merkle chains for every state transition

### What we've built (Apache-2.0)

[AgentMesh](https://github.com/imran-siddique/agent-mesh) provides a production-grade trust scoring engine with:

1. **5-dimension trust scoring** - Competence, integrity, availability, predictability, transparency
2. **Trust decay modeling** - Scores degrade over time without positive interactions
3. **Delegation chain validation** - Cryptographic proof of valid agent-to-agent handoffs (Ed25519 + DID)
4. **GovernancePolicy** - Declarative policies with YAML import/export, token/tool limits, blocked patterns
5. **Merkle audit chains** - Tamper-evident execution logs for compliance

### Proposed integration

A `langgraph-trust` package that provides trust-aware graph components:

```python
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph
from langgraph_trust import TrustGate, PolicyCheckpoint, trust_edge

graph = StateGraph(AgentState)

graph.add_node("research", research_agent)
graph.add_node("trust_check", TrustGate(min_score=0.7))
graph.add_node("execute", execution_agent)

# Only proceed to execution if trust score >= 0.7
graph.add_edge("research", "trust_check")
graph.add_conditional_edges("trust_check", trust_edge(
    pass_node="execute",
    fail_node="human_review"
))
```

### Why this matters for LangGraph

- **Enterprise adoption blocker** - Organizations can't deploy multi-agent graphs without governance guarantees
- **Natural fit** - LangGraph's checkpoint/state model maps perfectly to trust verification points
- **Composable** - Trust gates are just nodes; they compose with existing patterns (HITL, subgraphs)
- **Standards-aligned** - Implements CSA's Agentic Trust Framework zero-trust model

### Ask

Is there interest in this kind of integration? We could contribute:
1. A `TrustGate` node that works as a conditional checkpoint
2. A `PolicyCheckpoint` node that validates governance policies at graph transitions
3. Trust-aware edge conditions for `add_conditional_edges`

Happy to start with a minimal PR or a standalone package. Looking for feedback on preferred approach.

comments.author: hinthornw
comments.body: This would go in an external package, not in our core runtime.

comments.author: imran-siddique
comments.body:
Thanks @hinthornw! That's exactly what we were hoping to hear. We'll build this as a standalone `langgraph-trust` package that provides:

- `TrustGate` node (conditional checkpoint based on trust scores)
- `PolicyCheckpoint` node (governance policy validation at graph transitions)
- Trust-aware edge conditions for `add_conditional_edges`

All backed by [AgentMesh](https://github.com/imran-siddique/agent-mesh)'s 5-dimension trust scoring engine.

For context, we've already shipped similar integrations as external packages for:
- **Dify** (65K stars) — [merged into Dify Marketplace](https://github.com/langgenius/dify-plugins/pull/2060)
- **LlamaIndex** (47K stars) — [merged into llama_index](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/20644)
- **Microsoft Agent-Lightning** (15K stars) — [merged](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-lightning/pull/478)

We'll publish `langgraph-trust` to PyPI and share it here once it's ready. Appreciate the quick feedback!

comments.author: imran-siddique
comments.body:
Update: The `langgraph-trust` package is now built and available:

**[langgraph-trust on GitHub](https://github.com/imran-siddique/agentmesh-integrations/tree/master/langgraph-trust)**

### What's included (57 tests passing):

- **TrustGate** -- Conditional checkpoint node that evaluates trust scores. Supports min_score threshold, review_threshold for 3-way routing, and Ed25519 capability checks.
- **PolicyCheckpoint** -- Governance policy enforcement with token limits, tool allowlists/blocklists, blocked content patterns, human-approval gates.
- **trust_edge / trust_router** -- Drop-in condition functions for add_conditional_edges (pass/fail/review routing).
- **AgentIdentityManager** -- Ed25519 cryptographic identity (DIDs) with sign/verify.
- **TrustScoreTracker** -- Dynamic 0.0-1.0 trust scoring. Agents auto-blocked when score drops below threshold.

Only hard dependency is cryptography. LangGraph is optional -- nodes are plain functions returning dicts.

title: Preserve causal order for equal-timestamp checkpoints
body:
## Problem
When checkpoints share the same timestamp, read/list paths can return lexically ordered checkpoint IDs rather than causal/insertion order, making replay and debugging non-deterministic.

## Why now
High-throughput flows increasingly produce same-timestamp checkpoints, and deterministic replay ordering is required across checkpoint implementations.

## Evidence packet
- Commit under test: `c4f58611660543bf9341232eb971551654dcf5d0` (`origin/main`, 2026-02-19)
- Runtime environment: `Python 3.14.0`, `macOS 26.3`
- Minimal repro:
  1. Persist multiple checkpoints with identical `ts` values and different checkpoint IDs.
  2. Call latest/list APIs on sqlite/postgres savers.
  3. Compare returned order vs insertion sequence.
- Expected: stable causal ordering for equal timestamp checkpoints.
- Actual: query ordering is primarily by `checkpoint_id DESC`, which can reorder equal-timestamp writes lexically.

## Acceptance
- Add deterministic tie-breaking for equal-timestamp checkpoints in sqlite/postgres latest/list paths.
- Add regression tests for tie cases.

comments.author: preemalp
comments.body:
Hi! First time contributing here 

I looked into this issue and found the root cause - the ORDER BY clause 
in list() and get_tuple() uses checkpoint_id DESC as the only sort key. 
Since checkpoint IDs are random UUIDs, equal-timestamp checkpoints end up 
in unpredictable order.

I've opened a PR with a fix that adds a lightweight insertion-order 
tiebreaker - rowid DESC for SQLite and ctid DESC for Postgres. 
Both require zero schema changes.

PR: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/6871

Happy to get any feedback!

title: Lock collision-safe checkpoint key behavior for thread IDs across checkpointers
body:
## Problem
Checkpoint identity must remain collision-safe in multi-tenant usage; if key derivation ever regresses toward normalized-thread-only behavior, different tenant thread IDs could alias.

## Why Now
Tenant density is increasing and checkpoint correctness is a platform contract. We need explicit regression coverage so this guarantee cannot silently regress.

## Current Behavior Is Insufficient
Current implementations rely on composite keying (`thread_id`, namespace, checkpoint id), but this safety property is not clearly enforced by dedicated collision-focused tests across checkpointers.

## Why Code Change
This needs code-level contract tests and any small hardening required in key-construction paths; docs are not sufficient.

## Scope / Codepaths
- `libs/checkpoint/...`
- `libs/checkpoint-postgres/langgraph/checkpoint/postgres/base.py`
- `libs/checkpoint-sqlite/langgraph/checkpoint/sqlite/aio.py`

## Acceptance / Validation
- Add regression tests using collision-prone thread-id corpus (normalized-equivalent forms).
- Demonstrate no key aliasing and backward-read compatibility.
- Run checkpoint library format/lint/test gates.

## Repro Evidence Packet
- Version/commit under test: `origin/main` as of 2026-02-20.
- Environment: macOS (Darwin), Python/uv per repo setup.
- Minimal repro:
  1. Persist checkpoints for thread IDs that would collide under normalization-only schemes.
  2. Read each checkpoint back independently.
- Expected: independent retrieval, no overwrite/alias.
- Actual: contract is currently implicit; needs explicit non-regression coverage.

title: Entity-level merge for parallel branch state reconciliation
body:
When parallel branches in a graph modify code or structured state, reconciling changes at merge nodes is a known pain point. git's line-level merge creates false conflicts when two branches touch the same file but edit different functions.

[weave](https://github.com/ataraxy-labs/weave) is a semantic merge driver that merges at the function/class level using tree-sitter. It parses base/ours/theirs into semantic entities (functions, classes, imports), matches across versions, and merges at that granularity. Conflicts only happen when two branches change the same entity incompatibly.

On benchmarks: 31/31 clean merges vs git's 15/31. Supports 13 languages. Registers as a standard git merge driver via `.gitattributes`.

Also ships as an MCP server with tools like `weave_potential_conflicts` for detecting overlapping changes before merge and `weave_preview_merge` for simulating outcomes.

`brew install ataraxy-labs/tap/weave`

comments.author: Kelisi808
comments.body:
Nice proposal. One low-friction add that improved reliability for us:

- define a deterministic merge audit note per branch (`branch_id`, `state_keys_touched`, `merge_operator`, `conflict_resolution_path`).

Even when merge logic is complex, this makes regressions debuggable and lets QA replay branch behavior faster.

title: BinaryOperatorAggregate: Overwrite not unwrapped and duplicate-Overwrite guard skipped when initial value is MISSING
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangGraph rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import operator
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Annotated
from typing_extensions import TypedDict

from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START
from langgraph.types import Overwrite
from langgraph.channels.binop import BinaryOperatorAggregate
from langgraph.errors import InvalidUpdateError


@dataclass
class Metrics:
    count: int
    def __add__(self, other: "Metrics") -> "Metrics":
        return Metrics(self.count + other.count)


# Bug 1: Overwrite wrapper stored instead of unwrapped value when channel starts MISSING
class State(TypedDict):
    metrics: Annotated[Metrics, operator.add]

def reset_node(state: State):
    return {"metrics": Overwrite(Metrics(count=42))}

graph = (
    StateGraph(State)
    .add_node("reset", reset_node)
    .add_edge(START, "reset")
    .compile()
)

print(graph.invoke({}))
# Expected: {'metrics': Metrics(count=42)}
# Actual:   {'metrics': Overwrite(value=Metrics(count=42))}


# Bug 2: Duplicate Overwrite guard not enforced when first update is on MISSING channel
channel = BinaryOperatorAggregate(Metrics, operator.add) 
try:
    channel.update([Overwrite(Metrics(1)), Overwrite(Metrics(2))])
    print("NO ERROR (bug):", channel.get())
except InvalidUpdateError as e:
    print("Expected error:", e)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
No exception is raised. The incorrect output is:

{'metrics': Overwrite(value=Metrics(count=42))}
  Metrics(count=2)
```

### Description

When using `BinaryOperatorAggregate` with a type that has no default constructor, the channel sets `self.value` to
`MISSING`. In this case, passing an `Overwrite(x)` value to `update()` stores the wrapper object instead of the
unwrapped payload, so `channel.get()` returns `Overwrite(value=x)` instead of `x`.

On top of that, the `seen_overwrite` guard is never set in this code path, so passing two `Overwrite` values in the
same super-step silently succeeds instead of raising `InvalidUpdateError` as expected.

Both issues happen because the `MISSING` fast-path in `BinaryOperatorAggregate.update` skips the `_get_overwrite`
check that runs for all other values.

title: Align recency semantics across get_tuple, list, and history pagination
body:
Clients can receive contradictory latest/current checkpoint results across related APIs, causing replay bugs and incorrect synchronization logic.

Current behavior is insufficient because get_tuple, list, and history pagination can disagree under non-lexicographic IDs, so callers cannot depend on a single recency contract.

Why now: backend parity and durable replay correctness require one deterministic definition of recency.

Claim-to-codepath map:
- Read/query semantics in libs/checkpoint.
- Backend implementations in libs/checkpoint-postgres and libs/checkpoint-sqlite.
- Cursor behavior (before, limit) in history/list retrieval paths.

Requested behavior: all retrieval surfaces return consistent recency ordering semantics with focused cross-backend regression tests.

## Evidence Packet
- Commit under test: 6a2498a7
- Runtime environment:
  - OS: Darwin 25.3.0 arm64
  - Python 3.14.0
  - go version go1.25.7 darwin/arm64
  - Node: v22.19.0
- Minimal repro:
  1. Follow the repo's current local validation/CI-triage path.
  2. Observe the behavior described above for this issue.
- Expected behavior: deterministic, documented behavior matching acceptance criteria below.
- Actual behavior: behavior can be inconsistent for the scenario described above.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Implement the smallest code change that addresses the proven pain point.
- Add focused regression test coverage for the changed behavior.
- Ensure backward compatibility expectations are explicit in tests/docs.

title: get_subgraph fails when nodes share a common prefix
body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangGraph rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangGraph (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph

    class State(TypedDict):
        do_not_care: str

    def generic_node(state: State) -> State:
        # Just need a properly typed node; we will not be running this graph
        return state

    grandchild_graph_builder = StateGraph(State)
    grandchild_graph_builder.add_node("grandchild", generic_node)
    grandchild_graph_builder.set_entry_point("grandchild")
    grandchild_graph_builder.add_edge("grandchild", END)
    grandchild_graph = grandchild_graph_builder.compile()

    child_graph_builder = StateGraph(State)
    child_graph_builder.add_node("child_subgraph", grandchild_graph)
    child_graph_builder.set_entry_point("child_subgraph")
    child_graph_builder.add_edge("child_subgraph", END)
    child_graph = child_graph_builder.compile()

    parent_graph_builder = StateGraph(State)
    parent_graph_builder.add_node("common_prefix", child_graph)
    parent_graph_builder.add_node("common_prefix_2", child_graph)
    parent_graph_builder.set_entry_point("common_prefix")
    parent_graph_builder.add_edge("common_prefix", "common_prefix_2")
    parent_graph_builder.add_edge("common_prefix_2", END)

    parent_graph = parent_graph_builder.compile()

    # It's pretty intricate to get this to fail against the previous
    # implementation of get_subgraphs. You need the following conditions:
    # * A parent graph with 2 subgraphs
    # * Subgraph A added before subgraph B
    # * Subgraph A's name is a prefix of subgraph B's name
    # * Subgraph B must also contain a subgraph (call it subgraph C)
    # * You must call get_subgraphs with the namespace 'subgraph_b|subgraph_c'
    #
    # The old implementation used prefix matching to find subgraphs,
    # so it would chop of subgraph A's name from subgraph B's name and
    # look for subgraph C under the chopped-off name, which would fail.
    subgraphs = parent_graph.get_subgraphs(
        namespace="common_prefix_2|child_subgraph",
        recurse=True,
    )
    assert len(list(subgraphs)) == 1
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
(assert at the end of example code fails)
```

### Description

`Pregel.get_subgraphs()` had a subtle bug due to the fact that it matches node names with namespaces using startswith. This created the possibility (which I did in fact hit in production) that 2 nodes whose names share a common prefix, and both contain subgraphs, could cause the algorithm to malfunction. It would find the first node (whose name was a prefix of the second), chop off that many characters leaving a partial namespace, and recurse on that.

### System Info

This is a logic bug not affected by system info. I put up a PR to fix it: #6366

comments.author: xXMrNidaXx
comments.body:
Nice catch on the prefix matching bug! This is a subtle issue that can bite you in production.

**Workaround until fixed:**

Avoid node names that are prefixes of each other:
```python
# Instead of:
parent_graph_builder.add_node("common_prefix", child_graph)
parent_graph_builder.add_node("common_prefix_2", child_graph)

# Use unique names:
parent_graph_builder.add_node("process_a", child_graph)
parent_graph_builder.add_node("process_b", child_graph)
```

Or use a naming convention with unique suffixes:
```python
parent_graph_builder.add_node("node_alpha", child_graph)
parent_graph_builder.add_node("node_beta", child_graph)
```

**For the fix itself**, the matching logic should use exact delimiter-based matching instead of `startswith`:
```python
# Instead of:
if namespace.startswith(node_name):
    remaining = namespace[len(node_name):]

# Should be:
parts = namespace.split('|')
if parts[0] == node_name:
    remaining = '|'.join(parts[1:])
```

We've hit similar namespace collision issues in production multi-agent setups. For complex LangGraph architectures, check out our implementation patterns: https://www.revolutionai.io

Happy to share more workarounds if needed!

The root cause was that  matches  against node  without checking the separator boundary. The fix ensures the match includes the full segment by requiring .

title: Add SAP HANA Cloud community checkpointer to docs
body:
## Community Checkpointer: SAP HANA Cloud

Hi! I've built and published a LangGraph checkpoint saver for **SAP HANA Cloud**: [`langgraph-checkpoint-hana`](https://pypi.org/project/langgraph-checkpoint-hana/)

### Links
- **PyPI**: https://pypi.org/project/langgraph-checkpoint-hana/
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/stubborncoder/langgraph-checkpoint-hana
- **License**: MIT

### What it does
Implements the full `BaseCheckpointSaver` interface for SAP HANA Cloud, enabling conversation memory, human-in-the-loop workflows, time travel, and fault recovery for LangGraph agents running on SAP BTP.

### Why HANA?
Many enterprises run on SAP and their business data lives in HANA Cloud. This checkpointer lets AI agent state live alongside financial documents, master data, and transactional records — one database to manage, back up, and secure.

### Features
- Full sync + async interface (async delegates to sync since `hdbcli` is synchronous)
- UPSERT-based writes (atomic insert-or-update via HANA's `UPSERT ... WITH PRIMARY KEY`)
- Thread deletion for cleanup/GDPR compliance
- `from_conn_info()`, `from_env()`, and raw connection constructors
- Unit tests (mocked) + integration tests against real HANA Cloud

### Request
Would it be possible to list this as a community checkpointer in the LangGraph documentation (alongside Redis, Couchbase, etc.)?

Thank you!

title: Add explicit CI status classifier for LangGraph maintenance automation
body:
Problem
CI outcomes are consumed ad hoc in maintenance automation and can misclassify `no checks` states as pass.

Why now
Cross-repo reliability workflows require deterministic check-state categorization.

Current behavior is insufficient
Raw check rollups are heterogeneous and not normalized for automation consumers.

Expected behavior
Introduce a machine-readable classifier command/script that maps check rollups to normalized states.

Acceptance criteria
- Deterministic JSON output schema.
- Correct mapping for `failed`, `pending`, `no checks`, `policy-blocked`.
- Explicit handling for `gh pr checks` returning `no checks reported`.

Validation
- Unit/fixture tests for all states.
- Verification against at least one real PR in each category when available.

Codepaths
- `libs/cli`
- `scripts`
- `Makefile`

comments.author: Flave1
comments.body:

2. Return stable JSON output for automation consumers.
3. Handle the explicit `gh pr checks` “no checks reported” case.
4. Add fixture/unit tests covering each state.
5. Validate against real PRs where available and include results in the PR description.

comments.author: VisionExpo
comments.body: It appears the Studio frontend expects block.data to contain base64 content when type="file" and source_type="base64". However, the message block stored after upload contains "data": "", causing the renderer to throw No data found for file. Backend processing works correctly, so this seems to be a UI state rehydration issue rather than API failure. The renderer should either gracefully handle empty data or rely on a persisted file reference instead of inline base64.

comments.author: JiwaniZakir
comments.body: This caught my eye. I think I see what's going on here, let me put together a fix. I'll include a test to prevent regression.

comments.author: rotem1850
comments.body: @JiwaniZakir Waiting for your fix 🥇

comments.author: weiguangli-io
comments.body:
I have looked into this. The issue is in the Studio frontend's message rendering pipeline. When a PDF is uploaded via the chat UI, the message block is constructed with `type: "file"`, `source_type: "base64"`, and `data: "<base64>"`. However, after the message round-trips through the backend (stored and rehydrated), `block.data` comes back empty. The renderer then throws "No data found for file" because it expects inline base64 content.

The backend processes the file correctly (the agent can read the PDF), so the data is available server-side -- it is just not persisted or returned in the message block for the UI to render.

**Root cause:** The file content (base64 data) is either stripped during message serialization/storage or not included in the response payload sent back to the Studio UI. The renderer has no fallback for missing data.

**Proposed fix (two-part):**
1. **Storage layer:** Ensure the file block's `data` field is persisted when storing the message, or store a file reference (e.g., a content-addressable key) that the UI can use to fetch the file content on demand.
2. **Renderer fallback:** Even if (1) is fixed, the renderer should gracefully handle missing `data` -- e.g., show a file icon with the filename/mime type instead of crashing the entire conversation thread.

I see @JiwaniZakir mentioned working on a fix. If there is no PR yet for the renderer-side graceful degradation, I am happy to submit one.

comments.author: r266-tech
comments.body: I've submitted a fix for this in #7241. The root cause is that `asyncio.wait(tasks)` in `AsyncBackgroundExecutor.__aexit__` can raise `CancelledError` when the outer coroutine is cancelled during cleanup, which propagates out and prevents proper task inspection. The fix wraps it in a try/except to allow cleanup to complete.

> watchfiles: 1.1.1
> xxhash: 3.6.0
> zstandard: 0.25.0

This looks like cancellation propagation during AsyncExitStack cleanup. In Python 3.11+, CancelledError inherits from BaseException and will bypass except Exception. It may require explicit suppression in AsyncPregelLoop.aexit around asyncio.wait(tasks). Can maintainers confirm whether cancellation during streaming shutdown is expected behavior?

Happy to tackle this one. Working on it. I'll include a test to prevent regression.

Here's my fix: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/pull/7046 -- happy to iterate on feedback.

As a side note, this happens frequently in Cloud deployments on LangSmith, both Development and Production environments, but I am unable to reproduce it locally using `langgraph dev`.

It's great to see community interest in fixing these issues, but it would be very helpful to get some feedback or a status update from the LangGraph team as well.

@sydney-runkle

Following this.

**For others facing this**: pin to 1.0.8 as a temp solve until this is resolved. 

I've submitted a fix for this in #7241. The root cause is that `asyncio.wait(tasks)` in `AsyncBackgroundExecutor.__aexit__` can raise `CancelledError` when the outer coroutine is cancelled during cleanup, which propagates out and prevents proper task inspection. The fix wraps it in a try/except to allow cleanup to complete.

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.constants import START, END
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph
from langgraph.types import Command, interrupt


def ask_twice(state):
    interrupt("first question")
    interrupt("second question")


checkpointer = InMemorySaver()
builder = StateGraph(dict)
builder.add_node("ask_twice", ask_twice)
builder.add_edge(START, "ask_twice")
builder.add_edge("ask_twice", END)
graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)

config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}

graph.invoke({}, config)
graph.invoke(Command(resume="ans1"), config)

snap = graph.get_state(config)
print(snap.next)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell
No exception is raised. For above repro code, snap.next returns () instead of ('ask_twice',)
```

### Description

When a node contains multiple `interrupt()` calls (e.g., two interrupts in the same node body), `get_state().next` can incorrectly become `()` after resuming from the first interrupt and hitting the second. The graph is still paused waiting for input, but snapshot preparation replays `RESUME` pending writes into `task.writes`, so the snapshot logic excludes the node from `next`. As a result, anyone relying on `state.next` to determine whether the graph is waiting may mistakenly treat the run as complete.

comments.author: JiwaniZakir
comments.body: This is a known edge case with how LangGraph handles multiple `interrupt()` calls within a single node. After the first interrupt is resumed, the node re-executes from the top and hits the second `interrupt()`, but the checkpoint written at that point doesn't correctly record the node as pending in `next` — it ends up as an empty tuple even though there's still a pending interrupt. The `tasks` field on the state snapshot should still reflect the pending interrupt value, so `get_state().tasks[0].interrupts` can be used as a workaround to inspect the interrupt state until this is fixed. The root cause is likely in how `next` is computed from the checkpoint when an interrupt occurs during a node re-entry rather than a fresh entry.

comments.body: This is a known issue with how checkpoints record the "next" state after a node re-enters and hits a second `interrupt()`. The fix should ensure that when an interrupt is raised during a node's re-execution, the resulting checkpoint snapshot still reflects that node as pending in `next`, the same way it does on the first interrupt.

body:

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
import importlib
import os
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from langgraph.checkpoint.base import empty_checkpoint
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.checkpoint.serde.jsonplus import JsonPlusSerializer


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
    module_path = Path(temp_dir) / "temp_model.py"
    module_path.write_text(
        "from dataclasses import dataclass\n"
        "@dataclass\n"
        "class SavedObject:\n"
        "    value: int\n"
    )

    sys.path.insert(0, temp_dir)
    module = importlib.import_module("temp_model")
    SavedObject = module.SavedObject

    saver = InMemorySaver(
        serde=JsonPlusSerializer(
            allowed_msgpack_modules=(("temp_model", "SavedObject"),)
        )
    )

    config = {
        "configurable": {
            "thread_id": "thread-1",
            "checkpoint_ns": "",
        }
    }

    checkpoint = empty_checkpoint()
    checkpoint["channel_values"]["state"] = SavedObject(123)
    checkpoint["channel_versions"]["state"] = 1

    saved_config = saver.put(
        config,
        checkpoint,
        metadata={"source": "loop", "step": 1},
        new_versions={"state": 1},
    )

    sys.modules.pop("temp_model", None)
    os.remove(module_path)
    importlib.invalidate_caches()

    restored = saver.get_tuple(saved_config)
    assert restored is not None
    value = restored.checkpoint["channel_values"]["state"]

    # The restored value becomes None after deserialization failure.
    assert value is not None
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell

```

### Description

I'm using a LangGraph checkpointer to restore checkpointed state that includes a custom dataclass. In the example code, checkpointing succeeds first, then the original module is removed before the checkpoint is loaded again. I expect deserialization failure to either be surfaced explicitly or handled in a way that preserves the serialized value, but the restored value is silently replaced with `None`.

Also reproduced on `main` at `79a756`.
